turns.user: Daniel hurt himself in a fall at home last night. The hospital thinks he broke either his hip or the lower leg bone, they are still waiting on scans, and it looks like a closed fracture. What would his accident insurance give him?
turns.visible:
The Group Insurance Product Summary (page 13) pays the Simple Fracture as a percentage of the Simple Fracture Benefit Limit of S$5,000 for each listed case: Neck, Skull or Spine (Full Break) 100%; Hip 75%; Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee 50%; Cheekbone, Shoulder or Hairline Fracture of Skull or Spine 30%; Arm, Elbow, Wrist or Ribs 25%.
Which of these cases is it: Hip or Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee?

turns.user: Update: it is definitely the lower leg, the tibia.
turns.visible:
If the Simple Fracture benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee”, the conditional illustration is S$2,500: 50% of the Simple Fracture benefit limit of S$5,000, under the Group Insurance Product Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
If the Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee” (the row the document labels “Other Fracture”; these documents print no definition of which fractures that is), the conditional illustration is S$300,000: 50% of Daniel's sum insured of S$600,000 (Group Personal Accident), under the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
You told me it is definitely the lower leg, the tibia.
Both summaries describe these fracture benefits as applying to bodily injury resulting from an accident.
The Group Insurance Product Summary (page 13) prints “Simple Fracture” as a percentage of a fixed Simple Fracture Benefit Limit; the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary (page 8) prints “Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident” as a percentage of Daniel's own sum insured. Neither document says whether one amends, replaces or adds to the other, or which applies to this event, so these are alternatives from separate documents, never a total.

G. Ambulance Cost
If an Insured Person sustains bodily injury as a result of an Accident, which necessitates the use of an ambulance, we will reimburse the actual
ground ambulance costs on a per event per Insured Person basis, incurred by the Insured Person up to maximum of $500 for transportation
(including the medical supplies used) to the Hospital.
This Benefit can only be claimed either under the Core Scheme or Voluntary Scheme.

Section 5 - Compassionate Death Allowance Benefit
If an Insured Person dies as a result of an Accident, we will pay the funeral expenses incurred, up to $2,000,
on receipt of proof of death and the relevant documents in our prescribed form.
This Benefit can only be claimed either under the Core Scheme or the Voluntary Scheme.

If an Insured Person sustains bodily injury as a result of an Accident, which necessitates the use of an ambulance, we will reimburse the actual
ground ambulance costs on a per event per Insured Person basis, incurred by the Insured Person up to maximum of $500 for transportation
(including the medical supplies used) to the Hospital.
This Benefit can only be claimed either under the Core Scheme or Voluntary Scheme.

Section 5 - Compassionate Death Allowance Benefit
If an Insured Person dies as a result of an Accident, we will pay the funeral expenses incurred, up to $2,000,
on receipt of proof of death and the relevant documents in our prescribed form.
This Benefit can only be claimed either under the Core Scheme or the Voluntary Scheme.
